Subject: Post-call: TTFT & streaming constraints checklist + next steps

Emily — thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap and the action items we proposed on the call so we can lock the scope for a technical deep-dive: 

Summary of what we heard (high level)
- ClearPay needs a first-byte / first-token SLO for user-facing chat (mobile + web).
- Streaming responses are required for better perceived latency; preferred options are Server-Sent Events (SSE) or WebSocket depending on network resiliency.
- Peak concurrency and throughput are highly variable between markets; you called out some mobile-edge network constraints.

What we recommended on the call (items we can take/validate in a pilot)
1) Target TTFT goal: p95 <= 200ms for web; p95 <= 300ms for mobile degraded networks (baseline to discuss).
2) Streaming approach: prefer SSE for simplicity and proxy-friendliness; fallback to WebSocket when client needs binary frames or long-lived bidirectional.
3) Chunk cadence: target 150–250ms chunk cadence for interactive chat; consider larger chunks (up to 400ms) on mobile to reduce network overhead.
4) Throughput/concurrency: pilot with 200 rps / 300 concurrent streaming connections, then ramp to peak 800–1,200 concurrent depending on results.
5) Model & quantization proposals: we will suggest a few model variants (balanced latency vs quality) in the tech follow-up.

Action items (please confirm):
- Emily: confirm p95 TTFT target you care about for launch (web vs mobile) and provide a representative client distribution (percent mobile on 3G/4G/5G).
- ClearPay infra: share any WebSocket/SSE gateway constraints (timeouts, proxies) and a sample of production connection timeouts.
- Redwood (Ben/Aditya): provide a short runbook and SLO template (attached) plus a brief checklist of network traces we need.
- All: propose times for a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week (we listed a few below).

Attachments: SLO template (slo-template.xlsx) + network-trace request (we'll send).

Proposed deep-dive slots (PT): Tue 11/10 10:00–11:00, Wed 11/11 09:00–10:00, Wed 11/11 16:00–17:00.

If anything above is incorrect/missing, call it out and I will update. Thanks — looking forward to the follow-up.

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side so the pilot scope is aligned: 

Confirmations / corrections
- TTFT targets: our product team wants aiming for p95 <= 250ms for primary web clients, but the hard requirement is mobile where we operate under poor networks — for mobile we'd accept p95 <= 350ms as a realistic constraint. If you can show p95 <= 300ms on mobile with some client-side pacing, that would be ideal.
- Chunk cadence: 200–300ms is what our UX folks prefer on stable networks; on cellular we prefer 250–350ms to keep packets meaningful.
- Concurrency: average concurrency across regions is ~250; spikes to 1,200 qconns are possible during promos. We want to ensure graceful degradation rather than hard failures.

Network constraints
- Our edge uses an NGINX-in-front proxy with a 60s idle timeout by default (we can change per route).
- Some mobile carriers in LATAM rewrite chunked responses (we can provide examples).

Next steps for ClearPay
- I'll attach a small CSV with client distribution and a short sample of production socket timeouts.
- We prefer WebSocket if it buys us lower reconnects on flaky mobile; SSE is easier for our web clients behind standard proxies.

Proposed deep-dive slot: Tue 11/10 10:00–11:00 PT works for us. Please send a calendar invite.

Best,
Emily Zhang
Head of Platform — ClearPay

Emily / team — quick technical note ahead of the deep-dive with specifics we can validate in the pilot: 

Short answers to the requested items
- TTFT (first token) realistically achievable: 
  * Hosted sandbox (multi-tenant): p95 ~ 240–300ms depending on payload size and cold cache.
  * Dedicated/Dedicated GPU pool: p95 ~ 140–200ms with warm KV cache and optimized chunking.
- Model choices: recommend a small/medium coverage pair — "redwood-7b-q4" for quality vs latency and fallback "redwood-3b-4q" for constrained capacity. This is primarily to give you a predictable fallback path.
- Streaming framing & chunk cadence:
  * Aim for 150–250ms server-side emission cadence for interactive feel.
  * For mobile networks, coalesce tokens into ~250–350ms windows to reduce packet loss sensitivity.
  * Use SSE for web where proxies are standard; use WebSocket for mobile where TCP connection stickiness matters.
- Throughput & concurrency plan for pilot:
  * Start: 100 concurrent streaming connections, traffic-shaped synthetic load to mimic 250 qps.
  * Ramp: 100 -> 300 -> 600 concurrent over 10 business days, monitoring TTFT and token QPS.
- Instrumentation & tests needed from ClearPay:
  * Network traces (attached template: network-trace-req.txt).
  * Representative payload sizes (avg prompt tokens / max context).
  * Expected session length (median tokens per session).

Performance caveats:
- Cold KV cache will add 30–60ms to first-token in many cases; prefix caching reduces this significantly.
- If client-side token buffering is present (e.g., only display after N tokens), perceived TTFT will differ from server-side first-token. We will include guidance for minimal client-side buffering.

I'll upload a short runbook and a traffic generator script to the drive link Lauren included. We can validate p95 numbers in a dedicated pilot environment — happy to detail instrumentation (synthetic vs canary) in the deep-dive.

— Ben Carter
